What is Adobe Firefly?

Adobe's generative AI family, trained on Adobe Stock and public-domain content and marketed as commercially safe with IP indemnification. Integrated directly into Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro and Express as well as a standalone web app.

Best for

Commercially safe generation inside an existing Adobe design workflow.

Main features

  • Text-to-image, Generative Fill and Generative Expand in Photoshop
  • Text to Vector in Illustrator
  • Generative Remove and Extend in Premiere Pro
  • Text to Video and Text to Sound Effects
  • Firefly Boards for moodboarding
  • custom models trained on your brand assets (enterprise)
  • Content Credentials provenance tagging
  • third-party model access (Google, OpenAI, Runway, Luma) inside the Firefly app.

Practical use cases

  • Extending a photo background to a new aspect ratio
  • removing unwanted objects from product photography
  • generating on-brand vector assets
  • creating commercially safe marketing imagery where provenance matters
  • video object removal.

Who is it for?

  • Design and creative professionals already using Creative Cloud; enterprise brand and marketing teams needing IP-safe generation.

Pricing, free access & limits

Generative-credit based; bundled into Creative Cloud plans; standalone Firefly plans

Plans described in the source

Free plan with a small monthly generative credit allowance (historically 25 credits). Firefly Standard around $9.99/mo (about 2,000 credits). Firefly Pro around $29.99/mo (about 7,000 credits). Firefly Premium around $199.99/mo for very high volume. Creative Cloud subscriptions include generative credits by plan tier. Enterprise custom with custom models and full indemnification. Verify - Adobe has revised credit allowances repeatedly.

Free plan

Yes - free Adobe account includes a small monthly generative credit allowance.

Free trial

Yes - Creative Cloud and Firefly trials (typically 7 days) available.

Usage limits to consider

Generative-credit metered. Different operations cost different credits - video and high-resolution generation cost far more than a standard image. When credits run out, generation slows or stops until the next cycle. Credits do not roll over.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The only major generator offering genuine enterprise IP indemnification, which is decisive for regulated brands
  • training data provenance is defensible
  • Generative Fill in Photoshop is the single most-used generative feature in professional design work
  • Content Credentials support real provenance disclosure.

Limitations to consider

  • Raw image quality trails Midjourney noticeably for artistic work
  • credit system is confusing and allowances have been reduced over time to community frustration
  • locked into Adobe's subscription economics including annual-plan cancellation fees
  • prompt adherence is weaker than newer competitors
  • the standalone Firefly app feels secondary to the in-app features.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, InDesign, Express, Lightroom
  • iOS and Android

Languages

  • Prompts supported in 100+ languages including Arabic and French

API access

Yes - Firefly Services API for enterprise, with content generation and automation endpoints

Integrations and exports

  • Entire Adobe Creative Cloud, Adobe Express, Adobe Experience Manager, Frame.io, third-party models inside the Firefly app

Evaluation notes

Firefly's purchase case is legal safety and workflow integration, not output quality. For enterprises, the indemnification is often worth more than the pixels. Check credit consumption rates for video before budgeting.
